reviewed_contracts: Arena fixed/mixed semantics remain unchanged; phase workload has a distinct identifier.
Phase storage is prepared identically before timing; A requests seed history and B provider publications are prohibited and checked before/after.
Claim workload has fixed 2048x64-byte allocations, exact 1/32-domain budgets, checksum and independent release-permutation hash.
Claim release batch, release phase and complete workflow metrics remain separate; complete workflow includes preparation, thread construction and close.
Controllers stage one executable and exact selected runtimes, observe loaded module path, verify disk hashes, workload, completion, resource states and recomputed raw statistics.
Pairs alternate AB/BA, preserve raw JSON and stderr, do not retry or remove samples, and return nonzero for failure/incomplete receipt.
CI builds against installed SDK and runs small A/A functional pairs without a noisy speed threshold.

nonblocking_gaps.issue: New benchmark smoke receipt directories are not included in upload-artifact paths; add receipts or directories for durable CI evidence.
Wording that both sides must be overwrite-cache versus retained-shape describes the earlier experiment, but is too restrictive for the claim-index countercheck; identify it as historical.

limits: No new performance process, device operation, build, or test was started by this review.
Module path and disk hash are not mapped-page attestation or signed provenance.
Failure paths may retain process-local resources until exit and never establish normal cleanup.
Four-thread global release interleaving is scheduler-dependent; each thread has deterministic strided positions.
Arena workflow excludes preparation and close by existing contract; claim workflow is a distinct complete allocator round and cannot be pooled.
CI smoke success establishes installed consumer functionality, not performance or Android runtime qualification.
